topics.summary: HarborStatus now has a purpose: a client on the isolated lab network should receive the current status page from the intended server. Installing a package is only one step. A request crosses name resolution, network policy, a listening socket, a virtual host, filesystem access, and application behavior. This chapter turns those layers into a service you can test.

topics.summary: A daemon is a process that provides a background service. Modern daemons commonly remain in the foreground while systemd supervises them. “Background service” describes the operating role; it does not require the program to detach itself or end its command with &.

blocks.text: A daemon is a process that provides a background service. Modern daemons commonly remain in the foreground while systemd supervises them. “Background service” describes the operating role; it does not require the program to detach itself or end its command with &.

Separate installation, configuration, process supervision, and user-visible health. A package can be installed without a running process. A process can run without listening on the expected address. A listener can accept connections while returning the wrong website. Record one test for each claim instead of allowing a green service status to stand for all four.

Use the package’s service unit unless you have a specific reason to replace it. Vendor units can include environment setup, shutdown behavior, and security controls that a homemade unit omits. Review local differences through systemctl cat nginx before changing them.
Linux example — 19.1
Inspect the web daemon and its process identity.

systemctl show nginx.service -p MainPID -p User -p Group
ps -eo pid,user,group,comm

topics.title: 19.2 Ports and Sockets
topics.summary: An Internet socket combines an address, transport protocol, and port. A service listening on 127.0.0.1:8080 accepts local IPv4 connections, not connections arriving at the server’s network address. 0.0.0.0:8080 means all local IPv4 addresses, which can expose more interfaces than intended. IPv6 listening and dual-stack behavior must be checked separately.

blocks.text: The first command inspects TCP listeners and, with sufficient permission, their processes. The second sends an HTTP request. Neither establishes that a remote client is allowed through a firewall. Unix-domain sockets use a filesystem-associated address rather than an IP port; their access depends on path permissions and service configuration.

blocks.text: Apache organizes behavior through modules and configuration directives. In the RHEL family, the common package and unit name is httpd; on Ubuntu and Debian it is apache2. Their configuration directory layouts and module-enabling conventions differ. Do not copy a Debian path into a RHEL playbook and assume installation translates everything else.

Use the distribution’s configuration-test wrapper before reload: commonly apachectl configtest on RHEL-family installations and apache2ctl configtest on Ubuntu. Inspect virtual-host selection with the corresponding -S invocation. A syntax test checks configuration, not certificate trust, content correctness, or external reachability. Name-based virtual hosts allow several sites to share an address while retaining separate configuration. (R43)

Choose Apache or NGINX for this lab rather than installing both and competing for port 80. Either can serve a simple static site. Operational familiarity, required modules, and application integration matter more than declaring a universal winner.

blocks.text: Run the reload only after the test succeeds and after confirming the unit is already running. Reloading asks the existing service to apply configuration; starting a stopped service is a different action. NGINX’s master and workers coordinate configuration changes and ongoing requests. The application’s observable outcome still needs verification after reload. (R44)

nginx -T prints the complete configuration as well as testing it. That is useful for tracing includes, but its output may contain sensitive settings. Keep it in an appropriately protected incident record, not a public paste.

Merely enabling encryption does not establish trustworthy server identity.

blocks.text: TLS encrypts a connection and, when the client correctly verifies the certificate, authenticates the named endpoint. A certificate connects a public key to identities under an issuer’s policy. The corresponding private key must remain protected. Merely enabling encryption does not establish trustworthy server identity.

Check the requested name against the certificate’s Subject Alternative Name, its validity interval, the chain supplied by the server, and the client’s trust store. A .test lab name needs a deliberate private trust arrangement; it is not a candidate for an ordinary publicly trusted certificate. Chapter 33 uses an explicitly trusted, short-lived lab certificate and separates that exercise from production issuance.

Do not turn curl -k into a monitoring solution. It disables a control you should be testing. Distribute an approved CA certificate or supply an explicit trust file for a bounded lab test. Renewal also needs a deployment and reload path, not just creation of a new certificate file. (R45)

openssl x509 -in /etc/pki/tls/certs/harbor.crt -noout -ext subjectAltName

topics.title: 19.7 Reverse Proxies
topics.summary: A reverse proxy receives a client request and forwards it to an application. This can concentrate TLS handling and public listeners while leaving an application bound to a private address. It also introduces another failure boundary: the proxy can be healthy while its upstream is unavailable.

blocks.text: This example deliberately replaces, rather than trusts, a client-supplied forwarding chain at a single edge proxy. The application must trust such headers only from that proxy. The lack of a URI after the upstream address preserves the request URI here. Adding a trailing slash changes URI replacement behavior. blocks.text: An application needs an executable, dependencies, configuration, a runtime identity, a working directory, and a supervised lifecycle. Declare writable state separately from read-only release files. A Python virtual environment or a container image packages dependencies; neither supplies a backup strategy or an operational owner.

Distinguish liveness from readiness. Liveness asks whether a process should remain running. Readiness asks whether it can handle its intended traffic. A readiness check may include a critical dependency, but a dependency outage should not automatically cause every application instance to restart continuously.

For HarborStatus, serving a known page with the expected release marker is more informative than checking only that port 80 opens. Later, a dynamic service might require a bounded test transaction with cleanup. Keep health checks cheap, non-destructive, and explicit about the behavior they prove.

topics.summary: A worker serving static files needs to read those files, not edit them. Let a controlled deployment identity or root own release content, with the service receiving read and directory-traversal access. Give writable application state a separate directory with narrower ownership.

blocks.text: A worker serving static files needs to read those files, not edit them. Let a controlled deployment identity or root own release content, with the service receiving read and directory-traversal access. Give writable application state a separate directory with narrower ownership.

Do not change the packaged NGINX worker identity merely to match a tutorial. Common identities include nginx and www-data, but inspect the active configuration. Check every parent directory, not just the page. A readable file under a non-traversable parent is inaccessible to the worker.

Secret material should not share a directory exported as web content. A web configuration error should not transform an application’s backup, private key, or environment file into a downloadable object.

blocks.text: Before opening a port, establish which interfaces and source networks need it. Confirm console recovery and retain administrative access. On a firewalld host, inspect active zones and both runtime and permanent settings. On a different host, identify its actual firewall manager instead of adding another one.

Test from an approved remote client and, where authorized, from a source that should be denied. Local requests cannot establish the external rule’s behavior. A cloud network policy can block a connection that the host firewall permits, and a public interface can expose a service that seemed private in a one-interface lab.

Do not open an application backend port when only its reverse proxy should be reachable. The restriction should be true in the binding address, network policy, and documented architecture where practical.

An approved reverse proxy may require an SELinux policy interface allowing outbound connections. Inspect available booleans and the denied operation before choosing one. blocks.text: Trace one failing request through layers. First identify the exact URL, client location, time, and symptom. Then verify name resolution, route, listener, TLS, virtual host, content access, and upstream behavior as applicable. Record what each test bypasses.

A 403 response indicates the server processed a request and refused access under some rule; it does not uniquely identify Unix permissions. A 404 can arise from the wrong virtual host or routing rule rather than a missing release file. A 502 or 504 often directs attention toward the upstream path, but use the proxy’s error log to determine the actual failure.

Collect systemctl status, a bounded journal window, application errors, and a response body or header sample with secrets removed. Resist restarting several layers simultaneously: that destroys the comparison needed to identify the cause.
Linux example — 19.12
Combine configuration, listener, and request tests.

sudo nginx -t
ss -lnt
curl --head --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 10 http://127.0.0.1/
